newsitem.title: USA: Rigel sees Moose Mountain output in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Rigel sees Moose Mountain output in 1997.

text.p: Rigel Energy Corp expects production to begin in 1997 at its much-publicized Moose Mountain oil and gas discovery in Alberta after years of uncertainty, Rigel chief executive Don West said on Friday.

The discovery, made three and a half years ago in craggy, environmentally sensitive Kananaskis Country, could come on stream as early as next spring, West said at an investment confference sponsored by FirstEnergy Capital Corp and Merrill Lynch & Co.
"The best case scenario would be next spring and the worst case scenario would be next fall," he said.
Rigel has one-third interest in the play and Hutchison Whampoa Ltd unit Husky Oil Ltd has the remaining stake. Juninswest Energy Inc has an overrriding royalty on Rigel's stake.
Rigel expects its share of production from Moose Mountain to eventually hit a peak of 5,000 barrels per day, he said.
The first well, drilled three and a half years ago, made headlinen mounted over what looked like a major oil discovery.
However, because of the mountainous terrain, ecological concerns and opposition from environmental groups, testing of the discovery became a major headache for the partners.
An early attempt to test the first well by injecting the oil back into the ground failed. The companies were finally able to test it successfully last November.
To date, five wells have been drilled on three pads at a cost of C$2 milion to C$3 million per well. Four hit oil and one hit gas.
"I still think it's a great play -- I always did," West told Reuters. "It's just that it has taken a long time."
